tickets.title: A bar notice says what the job is doing, not which model runs it
tickets.what:
The notice zone of all three bars (Claude statusline, Codex tmux bar, pi footer) names the work,
not the model. Owner, 2026-11-17: the subagent display is not good enough; drop the model first. Today an item is
`✓ oracle [6.2-astra · high]`; two imps collapse into `◐ imp ×2`.

acceptance.text: No model and no effort in any notice item, in every bar look (the Stacked look's second row included).
A HUD job reads role + job title (the brief's heading, else the package), e.g. `◐ imp 状态栏TPS`.
A Claude subagent reads its type + the short description its Agent call gave, e.g. `◐ Explore 找通知生成处`; a Codex subagent its name + task when known. Missing facts are left out, never guessed.
A finished or failed item carries how long it ran, fixed at the moment it ended (`✓ imp 状态栏TPS 12m`); nothing in the zone ticks between refreshes.
`×n` groups only items with the same kind and the same words; two different imp jobs show as two items.
Narrow bars cut the title at a word before dropping the item; the role/type stays.
Main-path tests per client with synthetic transcripts/jobs; frame snapshots updated only where intended.

tickets.title: The pinned need names the job; HUD jobs and subagents look different; an unread report shows
tickets.what:
Owner, 2026-11-17 (notice items 4–6). Today a need is `! Work: 1 needs you`, English only, without
saying which job; a HUD job (own herdr tab) and a native subagent (inside this session) look alike; a finished job whose
report the owner has not read looks like any other finished job.

acceptance.text: A pinned need names the job: `! imp 首页修正 asks`. Several: the first one plus `+2`; when even that does not fit, `! 3 needs`. Nothing pinned when nothing is open. Bar language rules unchanged (bars stay English-only except the job's own title).
HUD jobs and native subagents differ at a glance (a mark or ink; designer's choice), in every bar look.
A settled HUD job whose report is unread carries an unread mark (e.g. `✓●`) until the report is read; read state comes from the same job reader the MCP uses (`report_unread`), no new polling.
Main-path tests: several needs at three widths, a HUD job beside a subagent, unread → read.
